hero.name: Madhushri Patil
hero.intro: I work on voice AI — building agents that talk to people in Kannada, Hindi and English, and figuring out where they go wrong. AI Engineering student at KLE Tech, graduating 2026.

about: I got into AI through robotics — teaching a machine to look at a field and tell which plants were sick. Somewhere between the camera and the wheels, I realised what I actually cared about was the interface: how a person and a system understand each other when neither speaks the other's language natively.

Voice is the honest version of that problem. Indian voice AI is harder than the demos suggest: accents shift mid-sentence, people code-mix Hindi and English freely, and callers answer three questions at once. Most of what I know came from listening to hundreds of real calls that didn't go to plan.

So I've ended up liking the unglamorous half of AI — transcripts, latency, the exact moment an agent misunderstands someone — and building the tooling that makes those moments findable instead of anecdotal.

work.role: Voice AI & Forward Deployed Intern · 6 months
work.body: Built a Kannada voice agent that asks callers structured questions and collects their information, then developed English and Hindi conversational agents on the Dialflo platform. Audited production calls to trace where responses and flows broke, and wrote the preprocessing and prompt-generation scripts that made each next version less wrong.
work.takeaway: Prompt quality mattered less than I expected; conversation design and knowing what "failure" means mattered far more. You can't fix what you can't measure, and nobody has time to listen to every call — that gap is what I'm building for now.

work.body: Designed the telemetry pipeline — every message, tool call, token and error captured as JSONL, queued in SQLite with WAL mode, synced to Postgres. Built the Docker harness giving every candidate an identical sandbox, packaged the agent as Bun-compiled single executables for macOS, Linux and Windows, and contributed shared agent logic to the npm monorepo.
work.takeaway: Agents are only as debuggable as their telemetry. Building the boring layer underneath taught me more about reliability than building the model layer on top.

work.body: Machine learning, deep learning, NLP, speech processing and robotics on paper. In practice: Python, C++, and evenings spent wiring LiveKit, Deepgram and ElevenLabs into things that talk back.

projects.title: Voice Call Audit Assistant
projects.body: Auditing voice calls typically means manually listening through hours of recordings  slow and hard to scale. Inspired by EkStep Foundation's voice AI testing framework, I built a proof-of-concept system that analyzes call transcripts, flags potential issues, and surfaces agent recommendations cutting manual review time for auditors.

projects.title: Talent Compass — Recruiter Workspace for Blue-Collar Hiring
projects.body:
Every morning, a staffing team in Hubballi-Dharwad gets 1,500 raw job listings and a pile of seeker profiles messy Excel files with misspelled towns, mixed-up qualifications, no coordinates.

Talent Compass takes that chaos and turns it into action. It reads the files, figures out what each column means, cleans the data, maps every location to real coordinates on OpenStreetMap, and splits "ITI/Diploma/SSLC" into matchable tokens. Within seconds, the recruiter sees a live map — blue circles for talent, orange for openings — and instantly spots where the gaps are.

Then one click: the system scores every candidate against every vendor — how far they live, whether their skills and salary expectations fit — and produces a ranked shortlist. The recruiter hits send, a WhatsApp message goes out, and the calendar starts tracking. Four days later, a reminder pops up. Follow up. Close the loop. Someone gets hired.

No spreadsheet juggling. No manual matching. Just upload, see, send, track

roadmap.title: Vapi for S2S — Real-Time Voice Orchestration Platform
roadmap.body: Most voice AI platforms like Vapi are built around traditional STT→LLM→TTS pipelines. S2S models skip that pipeline entirely but lose the hooks those platforms use for call transport, safety filtering, and state management along the way. This project rebuilds that orchestration layer natively for S2S: WebRTC streaming, real-time guardrails, call routing, and a monitoring dashboard for production voice agents.

roadmap.title: RL-Finetuned ASR for Real-Time Voice Agents
roadmap.body: Standard ASR models are trained for offline transcription accuracy, not the tradeoffs real-time voice agents need low latency, robustness to interruptions and noisy audio, and fast partial transcripts. This project fine-tunes an ASR model with reinforcement learning, optimizing directly for these production-relevant signals rather than word-error-rate alone

roadmap.title: Voice AI Evals  Upload, Test, and Score ASR, TTS & LLM
roadmap.body: Upload audio or voice samples , run them across multiple ASR, TTS, and LLM models, and get scored results back  so you can see which one actually performs best before you build on top of it.

thinking:
# My Thoughts on AI and the Future

I’ve been thinking about what kind of new jobs and roles will exist in the next 10 years, especially seeing how fast AI, coding, and companies are changing. I also wonder if there is an AI bubble, considering companies are spending billions on cloud infrastructure and data centres. At the same time, the amount of electricity and water these data centres need makes me question whether this growth is actually sustainable. Maybe the AI bubble could burst, but even if it does, I feel like the way we work and the kinds of jobs we have will change completely.
offscreen: I decompress with an embarrassing number of Subway Surfers runs — the only game I am objectively improving at.
